questiontext.text: What is the main purpose of unit testing?

generalfeedback.text: Unit testing focuses on testing individual pieces of code such as methods or classes.

answer.text: Testing the whole system with real users

feedback.text: This describes system or acceptance testing rather than unit testing.

answer.text: Testing individual pieces of code such as methods or classes

feedback.text: Correct. Unit testing verifies small pieces of functionality.
Network performance testing is part of performance or load testing.
User interface testing is normally part of system or integration testing.

questiontext.text: In Test-Driven Development (TDD), what is the correct order of steps?

generalfeedback.text: TDD follows a cycle of writing a failing test, writing code to pass the test, and then refactoring.

feedback.text: In TDD the test is written before the code.
Correct. Tests drive the implementation.
Refactoring happens after the code passes the tests.
Tests should be written before implementation in TDD.

questiontext.text: Which annotation marks a method as a JUnit test method?

generalfeedback.text: JUnit uses annotations to mark test methods and configure test behaviour.

feedback.text: This is not a JUnit annotation.
Correct. @Test marks a method that JUnit should run as a test.
This is not used to mark JUnit tests.
This is not a JUnit annotation.

questiontext.text: Which JUnit method checks that two values are equal?

generalfeedback.text: JUnit assertions verify that expected results match actual results.

feedback.text: This is not a JUnit assertion method.
This method does not exist in JUnit.

questiontext.text: What is the purpose of a test fixture?

generalfeedback.text: A test fixture prepares the environment and objects needed for testing.

feedback.text: Fixtures prepare the environment for tests rather than storing user input.

answer.text: To provide a fixed set of objects used by tests

feedback.text: Correct. Fixtures create objects that tests use.
Fixtures normally contain predefined objects rather than random data.
Fixtures organise test setup but do not improve performance.

questiontext.text: Which annotation prepares objects before each test runs?

generalfeedback.text: @BeforeEach runs before every test method and is typically used to initialise fixtures.

feedback.text: Correct. It runs before each test method.
This is not a standard JUnit 5 annotation.
This annotation does not exist in JUnit.
JUnit does not use this annotation.

generalfeedback.text: Independent tests ensure consistent results regardless of execution order.

feedback.text: Test independence does not affect execution speed.

answer.text: To allow tests to run in any order

feedback.text: Correct. Tests should not depend on each other.

answer.text: To reduce the number of tests needed

feedback.text: Independence does not reduce the number of tests.
Assertions are still needed to verify results.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is NOT part of the common test structure?

generalfeedback.text: Typical test structure is Setup → Execute → Assert.

feedback.text: Setup prepares the test environment.
Execute runs the code under test.
Correct. Analyse is not normally a defined test phase.
Assert verifies the expected result.

generalfeedback.text: Many programming errors occur at the edges of valid input ranges.

answer.text: They make the program easier to read

feedback.text: Boundary testing is about detecting errors, not readability.

answer.text: Errors often occur at the edges of input ranges

feedback.text: Correct. Boundaries are common sources of bugs.

answer.text: They reduce the number of tests needed

feedback.text: Boundary testing may actually increase the number of tests.
Testing strategy does not affect compilation speed.

questiontext.text: What is the main benefit of automated tests using JUnit?

generalfeedback.text: Automated tests allow developers to run tests frequently during development.

feedback.text: Correct. Automated tests help detect regressions quickly.
Testing helps find problems but does not eliminate debugging.
Testing improves quality but cannot guarantee zero bugs.
Automated tests are designed to run repeatedly.
